findings.evidence: sameVariables preserves nil versus empty and compares the actual right Dictionary stored key bytes using index(forKey:), then exact UTF8 values; whole RuntimeBookSnapshot equality also compares both URL bytes.

The existing replaceRecords path detects changed runtime snapshots, updates its bounded index, and admits noteAppChange to the existing persistence queue before the ordinary metadata writer. A key-only or value-only NFC/NFD edit now changes the actual revision.

noteAppChange uses exact map equality; identity, overlay applying and candidate snapshot equality use the same byte semantics. A genuine older snapshot cannot silently shadow this new accepted map through the normal writer.

Main publication accepts only the actual source/URL/revision and exact old-view or durable-owner variable maps. The changes introduce no new disk I/O, queue, file, library scan or App identity on Main; raw comparisons run on the existing bounded snapshot comparison path.

Two key/value branches use actual BookStore saveReadingBook, registered host metadata owner, ordinary progress writer, raw owned metadata bytes, stale asynchronous CAS refusal and normal reopen. Their expected values explicitly compare Data UTF8, not synthesized dictionary equality.

The raw URL case registers a genuine existing App grant, edits the same UUID via the actual normal save, checks the old lookup and old CAS are retired, and verifies exact URL bytes after a normal store reopen.

limits: No Swift typecheck/SDK/runtime result is established by this read-only review.
Same-App Dictionary representability remains finite; preview raw inputs need independent predecode alias guards.
Foundation atomic writes do not add explicit file/directory fsync or a power-loss guarantee.
